## Fixture Changes

- `web/e2e/helpers/payloads.ts` — `TurnActivityOpts.permissionMode` union widened from
  `"default" | "plan" | "acceptEdits"` to add `"auto"` (used by `rawUserPromptSubmit`/
  `rawPostToolUse`). Shape is unchanged — `permission_mode` is a plain string field on
  `UserPromptSubmit`/`PostToolUse` per canary-fields.md; `"auto"` is simply a fourth
  observed value from the plan's 2.1.259 probe, not a new shape.
- `web/e2e/helpers/session.ts` — `LaunchBody.permissionMode` union widened the same way,
  for `POST /api/sessions` request bodies built by `launchSession()`.
- No new fixture builders were needed: `envelopedSessionStart`/`rawUserPromptSubmit` were
  already generic enough to carry `"auto"`/`"default"` values without any new shape.

## Notes

- **REQ-6 (Should Have) is deliberately not covered here.** The plan's own Affected Files
  section marks it "web-tests' call; otherwise E4 covers it" for the unit-testable radio
  fallback logic (`setPermissionMode()`'s "no match" branch). E4 as written covers only
  the 4 *documented* stored values (`default`/`plan`/`acceptEdits`/`auto`), which are the
  only values reachable through the public API — `POST /api/sessions` validates
  `permissionMode` against exactly those four (REQ-2), and `repos.last_permission_mode` is
  set from that same validated request field, not from any later (unvalidated) hook value.
  There is no real-launch or synthesized-hook path that can put an unrecognised string or
  a literal `null` into a directory's `lastPermissionMode` short of writing to the scratch
  daemon's sqlite database directly — a pattern this suite's `helpers/db.ts` deliberately
  keeps read-only ("the E2E ingest oracle queries it read-only via the sqlite3 CLI").
  Inventing a write path for this one edge case felt like the wrong tradeoff against a
  Should-Have requirement the plan already routed to web-tests. If web-tests' agent
  determines `launch.ts`'s radio-selection logic isn't unit-testable in isolation, this
  gap should come back to e2e-specs at validate/fix time.
- E1/E2 launch through the real picker (`browseScratchDirectory` + `childEntry` click),
  matching the plan's User Flow 1 ("pick a directory, click auto, Launch") rather than
  hitting `POST /api/sessions` directly — REQ-1's radio and REQ-4's per-directory default
  are both dialog-level claims.
- E3 mirrors `sessions.spec.ts`'s existing "seeded in plan mode" test (E5 there) exactly:
  real launch → enveloped `SessionStart` bind → raw turn-activity hook → badge assertion.
  No new wire shape was invented; `permission_mode: "default"` on `UserPromptSubmit` is
  already a shape `rawUserPromptSubmit` produces today, just with a value the plan didn't
  use it for yet.
- D3/D4/D5/D6/D7/D8/D9 (daemon-side accept/reject/argv/repos/latch/grep) and W1/W2/W7 are
  outside e2e's scope per the plan's own Acceptance Criteria section — left to
  daemon-tests/web-tests and the Automated Checks block.

### REQ-6 coverage — explicit statement per the team-lead's ask

No honest E2E path exists for the null/unrecognised stored-value case, and I did not
add one. Verified independently in validate mode (not just carried over from the
authoring log's claim):

- `POST /api/sessions`'s request validation (`internal/server/sessions.go`, confirmed in
  `daemon-implementation.md`) accepts only the four documented values and 400s anything
  else (D4) — there is no real-launch path that can write an unrecognised string into
  `repos.last_permission_mode`.
- `repos.last_permission_mode` is set from that same validated request field (per the
  plan's Schema Changes and the daemon-impl log's note that `internal/store/repo.go`
  needed zero changes) — not from any later, unvalidated hook value — so no synthesized
  hook payload can reach it either.
- `web/e2e/helpers/db.ts` is confirmed read-only: it shells out to `sqlite3 -readonly`
  and exposes only `queryEvents`/`countAllEvents`/`countMigrations`/`countUsageSamples`
  (all reads, no write/exec helper). Writing directly to the scratch daemon's database to
  manufacture a null/unrecognised `lastPermissionMode` would mean adding a write path to
  a helper module the Protocol Contract itself documents as read-only-by-design — out of
  bounds for a repair, and not something I did.

REQ-6 (Should Have) is therefore still uncovered by E2E after this validate pass, exactly
as authoring flagged and as web-tests' log independently confirmed (`web-tests.md`'s "REQ-6
unit-testability" section, routing it back to E4 and finding E4 already covers the four
*recognised* values, not the null/unrecognised one). This is a real, permanent coverage
gap under the current API surface — not a missing test I could still write — and should be
recorded as such by the reviewer/orchestrator rather than assumed covered.
